title: Repossession and Collateral Recovery Expense Charging Rules
content:
Recovery Department rules for posting and removing recovery expenses on a Repossession and Collateral Recovery case.

## 1. When an expense may be posted

Recovery expenses are posted only on a case in recovered status. The test reads the case status on record; a case in pre-repossession review or assigned status, or one already closed, takes no new expense.

## 2. What may be charged

Every expense must be a reasonable expense actually incurred (reasonable expenses actually incurred in retaking, holding, preparing and disposing of the vehicle, itemised, UCC 9-615(a)(1)) and is charged from the collateral class schedule:

- the impound release administrative fee plus the impound lot's charges at their receipted amount, for a case whose recovery method is impound release;
- the transport fee, for every recovery method except impound release;
- the key replacement fee, only when no key was obtained at recovery;
- the auction fee, only when the vehicle actually sells;
- reconditioning backed by a vendor invoice, up to the class reconditioning cap.

| Recovery method | Transport fee | Impound administrative fee and lot charges |
|---|---|---|
| Involuntary recovery | charged | not charged |
| Voluntary surrender | charged | not charged |
| Impound release | not charged | charged (lot charges at the receipted amount) |

## 3. Retired clauses

The following parts of the original schedule are **no longer in force** and have been superseded by the current basis:

- "the involuntary repossession fee for recovery method involuntary recovery" — no longer in force;
- "the voluntary surrender fee for voluntary surrender" — no longer in force;
- "storage at the class storage fee per day for each chargeable day (the chargeable storage days, recorded as the days charged)" — no longer in force;
- "Storage is posted once, on the date the vehicle is released or sold, for every chargeable day up to that date." — no longer in force.

The class figures themselves stay valid and are read from the class expense schedule and rate card.

## 4. Definitions used with storage

- **Chargeable storage days** of one case: the calendar days from the day after the recovery date through the release, reinstatement, redemption or sale date inclusive, less the class free days, never below 0 and never above the class maximum of days charged.
- A **storage charge** figured on chargeable days is the class day fee multiplied by the chargeable days, rounded to the cent.

*Illustration with hypothetical figures:* recovery on 1 May and sale on 20 May give 19 days (2 May through 20 May); less 2 free days leaves 17 chargeable days; at a hypothetical day fee of 10.00 the storage charge is 170.00.

## 5. Removing an expense

An expense can be removed only once, and only with the removal reason assessed in error when it was charged outside this schedule or was not actually incurred; correctly charged expenses are never waived as a courtesy (courtesy waivers are not allowed in any class). A second removal of an expense already removed is not made: the removal record of that expense on the case is the test.
